title: Intent classifier + SLA estimator and evidence synthesizer for security/compliance asks
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a deterministic + ML-assisted pipeline that classifies incoming customer security/compliance asks (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA/GDPR/DPA/vendor questionnaires), suggests an SLA tier, and automatically composes a minimal evidence bundle draft. The feature should reduce manual routing time, provide transparent rationale for SLA decisions, and produce a curated evidence payload that can be reviewed and sent by the success team.
acceptance_criteria: Classifier reliably maps common questionnaire types to one of the pre-defined lanes (Fast-Track, Standard, Legal-Review, Executive-Escalation) with >88% precision on held-out historical requests.
SLA estimator outputs suggested response window (in hours) plus confidence band and lists the primary driver (e.g., db residency, regulated data, contract value).
Evidence synthesizer generates an ordered list of required artifacts and populates templates for standard asks (SOC2 controls mapping, data flow summary, DPA excerpt) with a preview for reviewers.
UI shows classification rationale and allows override with audit log entries.
End-to-end latency from intake to suggested SLA+evidence bundle is under 30s for text-based requests and under 2 minutes for uploaded questionnaire PDFs (OCR + parsing).
Automated routing rules send high-risk/low-confidence items to Legal or Security and create an internal ticket with the suggested owner and priority.
Telemetry emitted for classifier confidence, routing decision, evidence template usage, and reviewer overrides; metrics visible in Console dashboards.
Privacy & data residency flags are applied so no PII from customer attachments is stored in plaintext in the modeled outputs.
comments: 2025-10-01 Maya Chen: Initial ticket created after recurring customer support backlog spike — customers waiting multiple days for simple SOC2/DPA clarifications.
2025-10-03 Product discovery workshop with Security, Legal, and Customer Success. Identified four primary lanes and required evidence artifacts per lane.
2025-10-06 Engineering review: suggested building classifier as a combination of rule-based keyword matcher + small fine-tuned intent model; evidence templates should be stored in S3 with versioning.

2025-10-08 Legal feedback: ensure all generated evidence drafts are marked DRAFT and auto-sanitized for sensitive customer terms. Add 'requires_customer_consent' flag for any tenant-specific disclosures.
2025-10-10 Design: mockups for the reviewer UI and override flow posted to Figma (link below). Need a lightweight audit trail component.
2025-10-12 PM: Prioritizing integration with existing intake webhook and Slack notifier for high-priority lanes. Also exploring quota to limit automated exports of evidence artifacts.
2025-10-15 Engineering: high-level spike planned to benchmark OCR + parsing for vendor questionnaire PDFs; dependent on contract with OCR vendor for PII masking.
implementation_notes: Architecture: webhook listener -> preprocessor (PDF OCR + parser) -> rule-based matcher -> intent model (small transformers) -> SLA estimator (heuristic weighted scoring) -> evidence synthesizer (template engine + S3 manifest). Build feature flags to enable/disable ML path per account. Data handling: redact PII at ingestion, persist only artifact references and non-sensitive metadata. Add opt-out for accounts that require manual handling.
next_steps: Spin up discovery spike for OCR parsing performance (ENG).
Security & Legal to sign off on data retention and DRAFT labeling rules.
Design to finalize reviewer UI and audit trail microcopy.
Create initial training set from last 18 months of intake tickets and annotate lanes (PM + CS).
Schedule kick-off with dedicated capacity team to discuss rate limits and autoscaling for batch evidence generation.
